project.name: shorts-uploader-engine
project.type: script-driven media upload automation with Electron desktop UI
project.summary: A repository for discovering local Valorant clips, generating metadata and derived assets, uploading to YouTube Shorts and Meta Reels, and auditing live platform uploads against local inventory. It uses root-level Python scripts plus two desktop UI layers: a Tkinter launcher and an Electron + React app.

youtubeBatchUpload.py.role: Primary orchestration script for upload workflows, Shorts conversion, metadata generation, YouTube publishing, and optional Meta cross-posting.

metaBatchReelsUpload.py.role: Instagram and Facebook reels publisher built on Meta Graph API using YouTube-uploaded items as source inventory.

generateLiveUploadAudit.py.role: Fetches live platform uploads and compares them against local video inventory, producing audit snapshots and comparison output.

rebuildUploadComparison.py.role: Recomputes upload_comparison.json from saved audit snapshots without making network calls.

generateUploadStatusReport.py.role: Builds a local aggregate report of total clips and per-platform upload coverage.

youtubeFixRepeatedMetadata.py.role: Maintenance utility for correcting repeated or problematic YouTube metadata.

musicOverlaySample.py.role: Utility/experimental script for music inventory and background audio overlay workflows.

projectUiLauncher.py.role: Tkinter desktop launcher that wraps script CLIs, validates inputs, previews commands, and streams output.

app/electron/main.js.role: Electron main process bootstrap for the Content Command Center desktop app.

app/electron/preload.js.role: Renderer bridge exposing safe APIs from Electron to the React frontend.

app/electron/services/uploadService.js.role: Runs Python upload scripts as child processes, tracks status, and streams logs back to the renderer.

app/electron/services/dataService.js.role: Reads root JSON state and ledgers to build video rows and status summaries for the Electron UI.

app/electron/services/pathService.js.role: Resolves repo paths, renderer build path, and the active video root.

app/useAppStore.js.role: Central Zustand store for page state, logs, upload status, metadata editing, and video filtering.

README.md.role: Human-facing operational overview and setup guide.

app/electron/ipc/systemHandlers.js.role: Add IPC handlers for loading and saving Electron UI workflow settings so the renderer can persist advanced upload configuration.

docs.title: Shorts Uploader Engine
docs.summary: # Shorts Uploader Engine This repository automates a Valorant short-form video pipeline: discover local source clips generate metadata upload to YouTube Shorts cross-post to Instagram and Facebook Reels audit live platform uploads against the local video library ## Content Command Center The repository now also contains a modular Electron + React desktop app under named Content Command Center. Current UI stack: Electron main process with preload bridge and IPC handlers React renderer with state-based page routing Zustand for shared UI state Framer Motion for transitions and interaction feedback Current UI modules: page modules for Dashboard, Library, Upload, Console, Audit, and Metadata Current UI behavior: renderer does not access Node directly preload exposes a safe Electron communication uses and Electron main can launch the existing Python scripts and stream stdout/stderr to the UI Library and Audit screens read the existing JSON state and ledger files the Tkinter launcher still exists and remains supported ## Desktop UI ### Tkinter launcher for the existing scripts. Responsibilities: expose the available CLI arguments as form fields validate common input combinations before launch show the exact generated command before execution stream script output live in the UI console persist the last-used values for each tab in Covered scripts: Typical usage: Behavior: saved form values are restored on the next launch scripts are launched unbuffered so the UI console updates progressively during long runs the UI wraps the existing scripts and does not replace their CLI entry points ## Main Scripts ### Primary YouTube uploader.

docs.title: AGENT_CONTEXT
docs.summary: # AGENT_CONTEXT ## Purpose This repository is a script-driven pipeline for uploading Valorant gameplay clips as short-form content to: YouTube Shorts Instagram Reels Facebook Reels It also includes reporting and audit tooling for comparing the local clip library against live platform upload data. The repository now has two operator-facing UI layers: the existing Tkinter launcher in a newer Electron + React desktop app in named Content Command Center ## Architecture The core automation architecture is still file-based and script-centric. There is no application framework, package layout, or database.

docs.title: AI Understanding
docs.summary: # AI Understanding ## Project Summary is an operations-focused repository for publishing Valorant clips as short-form video content across YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and Facebook Reels. The repository is centered on Python scripts and local JSON state files rather than a packaged backend application or database-backed service. It also contains two desktop operator interfaces: a mature Tkinter launcher in a newer Electron + React desktop app in The core mental model is: discover local source videos identify each clip by a stable file key generate metadata and derived media artifacts upload to one or more platforms persist local state and upload ledgers audit live platform inventories against the local library ## Architecture Summary ### Script-first automation The repository's primary business logic lives in top-level Python scripts: There is no shared Python package layout.

docs.title: Electron UI Implementation Plan
docs.summary: # Electron UI Implementation Plan This plan turns the missing-feature analysis into a practical bridge + Aider workflow. Goal: bring the Electron + React UI closer to operational parity with the existing script surface implement features one by one in small, reviewable changes keep progress visible in ## Recommended Execution Mode Use the bridge in: Why: one-file tasks fit the current bridge design best manual-supervisor keeps architectural review local approved tasks can be committed in small recoverable steps ## Execution Order ### Phase 1: Foundation add a shared Electron-side persisted settings model extend preload and IPC so the renderer can read and save upload settings expand upload command building to consume real operator inputs instead of hardcoded defaults ### Phase 2: Core Upload Parity add root-path, batch-size, privacy, playlist, and queue-filter controls add ffmpeg / ffprobe controls add credential and Meta ID controls add advanced metadata and music settings add dry-run and validation-friendly behavior ### Phase 3: Standalone Tool Coverage add flows for: metadata fix music sample upload status report rebuild upload comparison live upload audit ### Phase 4: Page Upgrades upgrade Audit to use real audit artifacts upgrade Metadata so it persists or is explicitly workflow-backed upgrade Library with search, sorting, and richer details upgrade Console with better run utility upgrade Dashboard with action shortcuts ### Phase 5: Reliability add setup diagnostics and environment checks align Electron state persistence with Tkinter launcher expectations review remaining parity gaps and update ## Review Rule After each completed feature: mark the feature in add a one-line completion note if the implementation changed scope, update the matching feature brief in ## Suggested Review Questions For each feature task, check: does the UI actually expose the missing capability does the renderer persist or send the right value does preload / IPC pass it safely does or

docs.title: Advanced AI Metadata Settings
docs.summary: # Advanced AI Metadata Settings The Electron UI only has a simple "AI Metadata" toggle and misses the advanced metadata controls already supported by the script. Notable missing options: OpenAI model channel name hint Instagram / YouTube username cross-link fields extra keywords language category ID notify subscribers AI uniqueness window AI metadata retry count Why it matters: metadata quality is a major part of the upload pipeline these values influence output style and publishing behavior Expected outcome: advanced metadata section in the upload flow persisted operator defaults support in command preview and process launch
